children: 2124 ET - Bitcoin pops back above the closely watched $60,000 mark in early trade, in line with a rebound in tech and AI stocks. The cryptocurrency has been moving in tandem with the equities selloff as both are sensitive to risk appetite and interest-rate expectations. Bitcoin's morning gains follow a drop overnight after U.S. inflation data firmed up Fed rate-hike bets, suggesting that dip-buying could be kicking in. Still, the outlook remains fragile. Tighter global financial conditions and the likelihood of more selloffs fueled by concerns about the sustainability of the AI trade suggest that a lasting rebound in crypto will be challenging. Bitcoin rises 1.1% to $60,889, but stays stuck at four-month lows. (fabiana.negrinochoa@wsj.com)

2046 ET - Long-term Japanese government bond yields are higher as sharp gains in semiconductor and artificial intelligence-related stocks hurt demand for government bonds as safe-haven assets. Stronger-than-expected 3Q U.S. GDP and elevated U.S. inflation data keep expectations intact for further rate increases by the Federal Reserve. That in turn could raise the prospects of the Bank of Japan's continued tightening. Earlier Thursday, BOJ board member Naoki Tamura said the central bank should bring its policy rate to neutral levels soon, as financial conditions are still accommodative. The 10-year JGB yield is up 1.5 basis points at 2.660% and the 5-year yield is 3.5 basis points higher at 2.080%. (kosaku.narioka@wsj.com; @kosakunarioka)

2046 ET - The Indian rupee looks set for further gains into 2027 as lower crude prices reduce oil importers' demand for dollars, OCBC FX strategist Sim Moh Siong says in a note. Improving equity inflows as investors rotate away from artificial-intelligence-heavy markets will also add to the rupee's gains, Sim says. The Reserve Bank of India is likely to use periods of rupee strength to rebuild foreign-exchange reserves, which should temper the pace of appreciation. OCBC forecasts the dollar at 92.10 rupees by the end of 2027. The rupee closed 0.7% higher at 92.23 against the dollar on Wednesday, according to LSEG data.(venkat.pr@wsj.com)

2036 ET - Asian currencies consolidate against the dollar in early trade, but may be weighed by risk-off sentiment. Mounting doubts over the sustainability of the artificial intelligence trade rattled Wall Street for a second straight day on Wednesday, UOB's Global Economics & Markets Research team says in a note. Investors are navigating concerns over the sustainability of the AI investment boom, rising borrowing costs and renewed tariff risks, Commerzbank Research analysts say in a note.The U.S. dollar is little changed at 159.09 yen and flat at 1.2901 Singapore dollars, while the Australian dollar is 0.2% higher at US$0.6638, according to LSEG data.(amanda.lee@wsj.com)President Emmanuel Macron has suggested a "golden rule" to balance the budget, ING's Chris Turner says. "Euro Could Stay Weak Against Dollar For Now — Market Talk," at 0841 GMT Wednesday, misspelled President Macron's name.

2021 ET - There are good reasons to think the Bank of Korea's tightening cycle is either nearing its end or already over, Capital Economics says after the central bank delivered its third rate hike of the year. The BOK's main concern is inflation, which has remained above its 2% target since the conflict in Iran began, says economist Gareth Leather. As base effects from the energy shock fade, Leather expects inflation to fall back toward the target early next year. Growth has also been concentrated in capital-intensive sectors and strong increases in productivity have helped prevent rapid GDP expansion from generating significant domestic price pressures. The won's strong rebound will also help ease concerns about imported inflation. (fabiana.negrinochoa@wsj.com)

2020 ET - The risk-reward of chasing dollar gains looks less attractive, but the prospect of a more hawkish Fed should keep the greenback supported, OCBC FX strategist Sim Moh Siong says in a note. The dollar's relation with stocks could remain choppy, caught between safe-haven demand and concerns that a deeper artificial-intelligence slowdown could weigh on U.S. growth, Sim says. A December Fed rate-hike is priced in on strong growth and sticky inflation, but a 50 bps move looks unlikely as the stock selloff has already tightened financial conditions, the strategist says. The ICE U.S. Dollar Index is up 0.1% at 103.73, according to LSEG data. (venkat.pr@wsj.com)

1916 ET - Japanese stocks are higher, rebounding from Wednesday's sharp declines, thanks partly to signs of U.S. economic strength. Semiconductor and metals stocks are leading the gains. Kioxia Holdings is up 11%, SoftBank Group is up 5.3%, and Sumitomo Metal Mining is 4.9% higher. The dollar is at 159.11 yen, compared with Y159.38 as of Wednesday's Tokyo stock market close. Investors are focusing on crude oil prices and bond yields. The Nikkei Stock Average is up 1.3% at 57745.27. (kosaku.narioka@wsj.com; @kosakunarioka)

1853 ET - Japanese stocks may rise following Wednesday's selloff and on signs of U.S. economic strength. Nikkei futures are up 0.9% at 57465 on the SGX. U.S. gross domestic product grew at an inflation-adjusted 4.3% annual rate in the third quarter, revised higher from its initial estimate of 3.4%. The dollar is at 159.21 yen, compared with Y159.38 as of Wednesday's Tokyo stock market close. Investors are focusing on crude oil prices and bond yields. The Nikkei Stock Average fell 2.8% to 57011.62 on Wednesday. (kosaku.narioka@wsj.com)

1805 ET - News that Australia's inflation problem got worse in October has scattered economists a little. Fitch Ratings now says the RBA will keep the official cash rate at an 18-year of 4.85% throughout 2027. Elsewhere, ANZ has brought forward its forecast for the first rate cut to June from August. In a world of slow growth and sticky inflation, the split is understandable. It will sharpen the focus on a speech by RBA Governor Michele Bullock next week. She's been hawkish lately. It's likely she will remain in that camp, watching the data flow intently. (james.glynn@wsj.com; @JamesGlynnWSJ)

1059 ET - U.S. artificial intelligence companies are expected to supply more debt in the euro market in 2027, after a record supply so far this year, CreditSights analysts say in a note. Euro investment-grade credit supply by U.S. based companies has risen to almost 160 billion euros in the year to date, the analysts say. Large U.S. AI companies looking to diversify their liabilities are likely to issue bonds in the euro market, they say. (miriam.mukuru@wsj.com)

1040 ET - The recent tightening in financial conditions has been cited as doing some of the work for the Federal Reserve, but inflation remains the primary driver of monetary policy decisions, says Michael Skordeles, head of U.S. economics at Truist. "It's on the radar. It's not a key piece," he tells WSJ. "These inflation prints, on the other hand, are a key piece," he says after the October PCE report came in above the Fed's target. "Financial conditions, of course, bleeds into that mindset, and they factor it in, but I don't think it's the top-of-mind main thrust of why they're going to move," Skordeles adds, further highlighting that inflation has remained above the Fed's target for several years. (jessica.coacci@wsj.com)
